mod: Stratagem Hero Expanded v1.0 (Vanilla Plus Megapack option)

source.why: checkout is at tag v1.0 (commit 381f9a1) and every file in components.lock.json source_sha256 matches it (the pinned copy in VanillaPlusMegapack/components/StratagemHeroExpanded is identical)

non_data_edits.new: local MEM_COMMIT, MEM_IMAGE, MEM_MAPPED = 0x1000, 0x1000000, 0x40000 ... (region.type ~= MEM_IMAGE and region.type ~= MEM_MAPPED)
non_data_edits.why: Mod.image_writable refuses any page whose VirtualQuery type is not MEM_IMAGE. Under the Proton build this game runs on, VirtualQuery reports game.dll's own image pages as MEM_MAPPED (0x40000), so the unmodified check would refuse the arcade tables and the mod could never apply on this machine.

evidence.observation: five game.dll image regions (rva 0x167F000..0x168C000, prot 0x1/0x20) report type 0x40000 MEM_MAPPED, state MEM_COMMIT, in the running game

text: applied (108 stratagems in 8 groups; pages 0x08, 0x08), at load.
evidence.note: the installed copy (PORT51 port carrying this same edit) applied on the tables' pages, which reported PAGE_WRITECOPY (0x08), i.e. section-backed image data, and held to shutdown

evidence.offline: under the workspace Wine (build.py --tests, out/TESTS.json wine_host_region_types) a normally loaded image (the test luajit.exe) reports MEM_IMAGE (0x1000000) for every section, and the unmodified upstream "page check" test passes there. So MEM_MAPPED is not generic Wine behaviour: it is how game.dll is mapped in this game under Proton, observed live only. The edit therefore adds MEM_MAPPED instead of replacing MEM_IMAGE, and live check H5 must confirm it on the tables' own pages.

non_data_edits.kept: MEM_COMMIT state, writable protection set {0x04,0x08,0x40,0x80}, region allocation base == game.dll base, exact vanilla bytes of both tables, every pool identity; MEM_PRIVATE and foreign-module pages still refused
non_data_edits.confidence: medium: observed live on other game.dll pages (same mapping), not yet on the tables' own pages (H5)
